# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 28/2/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Google introduces Nano Banana 2, combining advanced reasoning and image quality of Nano Banana Pro with faster generation speeds, outperforming other models in text-to-image generation.
- Anthropic refuses to remove safeguards in its models despite the Department of War's request, citing potential risks to democratic values, and stresses its commitment to using AI to defend democracies.
- Hyperscaler capital expenditures have quadrupled since GPT-4's release, nearing half a trillion dollars in 2025, highlighting the industry's rapid investment in AI and related technologies.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- **Nano Banana 2**: Google's new model combines the advantages of Nano Banana Pro with significantly faster generation speeds, enhancing AI capabilities.
- **Claude Code Update**: Anthropic updates Claude Code with auto-memory, allowing the AI coding agent to save project context and workflow preferences across sessions.
- **Hermes Agent**: Nous Research releases an open-source AI agent that gets smarter over time and connects to messaging apps.
- **PhFL**: Researchers propose a framework for phishing email detection using heterogeneous federated learning, addressing bias and class imbalance.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- **Algolia Agent Studio**: A platform for developers to build and test AI agents with built-in support for retrieval, augmentation, and generation (RAG) and multimodal chain-of-thought (MCP).
- **Wispr Flow**: A voice-to-text tool available on Android, offering users the ability to speak naturally and get clean text ready to send in any app.
- **Ticketify**: Turns messy bug reports into structured PM tickets, including steps to reproduce, acceptance criteria, and time estimates.
- **Pagesmith.AI**: Generates HTML-first Astro sites with built-in CMS and database, built for SEO and GEO indexing instead of JavaScript bloat.

## 📰 Industry News
- **Block Layoffs**: Block, founded by Jack Dorsey, lays off 40% of its workforce as part of a remake to focus on AI tools.
- **xAI Co-Founder Departure**: Toby Pohlen, co-founder of xAI, departs the company, marking the seventh co-founder to leave in less than three years.
- **OpenAI's Market Share**: OpenAI's daily US mobile user share drops from 69% to 45% from January 2025 to January 2026, while Gemini's and Grok's shares rise.
- **Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery**: Netflix walks away from a deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery's studio and streaming assets after Paramount's revised bid is deemed superior.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- **Guide to Keeping AI Hallucinations at Bay**: A guide on grounding AI to prevent hallucinations, covering what AI hallucinations are, why they happen, and methods for prevention.
- ** Tutorial on Setting Up a Codebase for Agents**: A tutorial on setting up a codebase for AI agents, including using "deep modules" to hide complex logic and applying classic software design principles.
- **eBook on Diagnosing AI Latency**: An eBook on diagnosing AI latency, providing insights into why AI models can be slow and how to optimize their performance.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- Samsung gives Perplexity system access, integrating search, writing assistance, and page summarization into the S26 experience.
- Anthropic refuses the Pentagon’s ultimatum, maintaining safeguards on mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.
- Google releases Nano Banana 2, a new image model with Pro-level quality at Flash speed.
- Unitree's G1 humanoid robots perform a synchronized kung fu routine, demonstrating autonomous capabilities.

### Detailed Points
- **Anthropic Refuses Pentagon's Ultimatum**: Anthropic published a formal response to the Pentagon’s ultimatum, refusing to lift guardrails on mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. If forced out, Anthropic says it’ll help with the transition, but the safeguards stay.
- **Samsung and Perplexity Integration**: For the first time, Samsung is giving system-level OS access to an app that isn’t made by them or Google. The integration bakes search, writing assistance, and page summarization directly into the S26 experience.
- **Google's Nano Banana 2**: The new image model brings Pro-level quality at Flash speed, with 4K output, subject consistency across up to five characters, and real-time web grounding. It’s rolling out across Gemini, Search, Flow, Ads, and the API now.
- **Unitree's Humanoid Robots**: Unitree's G1 robots performed a fully synchronized kung fu routine, with nearly fifty robots at Beijing’s Temple of Heaven. This follows two other viral demos: the Spring Festival Gala’s world-first autonomous cluster kung fu performance and a -53°F extreme cold walk.
- **Other Tools and Developments**:
  - **Pagesmith.AI**: Generates HTML-first Astro sites with built-in CMS and database, built for SEO and GEO indexing instead of JavaScript bloat.
  - **GoFaceless**: Creates short-form videos from a topic, with AI script, voiceover, visuals, captions, and music, ready to post.
  - **Solido**: Sends AI-generated invoice reminders from your own email, synced with Xero, with rules you control for timing, tone, and recipients.
  - **Ticketify**: Turns messy bug reports into structured PM tickets, including steps to reproduce, acceptance criteria, and time estimates.
  - **Mnemom**: Gives AI agents cryptographic integrity certificates so you verify safety judgments with math, not trust.
- **Brand Radar**: Tracks your brand mentions across all platforms (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google, YouTube, TikTok, and Reddit) in one view.
- **Meta’s Superintelligence Lab**: Alex Wang explains why Meta created a “Superintelligence” lab and why he’s deliberately slowing down.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from Nankai University, China, proposed a framework for phishing email detection using heterogeneous federated learning, allowing nodes to train locally and share model features without exposing private email content.
- The framework, called PhFL, addresses bias in response to data heterogeneity and class imbalance, and outperformed nine other baselines in experimental evaluations.
- PhFL uses a local representation model and a shared global classifier, with class feature-means calculated as the average of feature vectors produced by the local representation model.
- The system showed strong detection performance even in heavily imbalanced scenarios, and scaled well with the number of clients.

### Detailed Points
- The paper discusses the challenges of distributed security systems, particularly in the context of email protection, where privacy regulations prevent the sharing of raw email content.
- The authors demonstrate that existing collaborative phishing detection systems are limited by privacy constraints, and propose a framework that allows nodes to share intelligence without violating privacy.
- PhFL consists of two components: a local representation model that processes email text and converts it into low-dimensional feature vectors, and a shared global classifier that is trained on class feature-means uploaded by clients.
- The local training process incorporates a loss function that combines standard classification loss with a contrastive learning component, encouraging local class feature-means to align with global class feature-means.
- The server performs weighted aggregation of classifier parameters and class feature-means, and retrains the aggregated global classifier using the original class feature-means as training data.
- Experimental evaluations showed that PhFL outperformed other baselines in three scenarios with progressively more extreme imbalance, and that removing either architectural component noticeably degraded performance.
- The paper provides detailed derivations for the loss functions and aggregation procedures, and includes additional tests that demonstrate the system's scalability and performance.

- Google's Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) combines the advantages of Nano Banana Pro with significantly faster generation speeds, enhancing AI capabilities.
